root_cause: Commit 7a38204 ('fix for panel title') split the border style into partial_border_style (border_style only) and border_style (panel style + border_style), then stylized the title/subtitle Text with only partial_border_style. The panel's own `style` (e.g. 'on blue' background) therefore never reached the title/subtitle, so they rendered without the panel background (issue #3569: title 'white on dark' instead of 'white on blue').
best_solution: In Panel.__rich_console__ (rich/panel.py), revert 7a38204: drop partial_border_style, compute border_style = style + console.get_style(self.border_style), and call title_text.stylize_before(border_style) and subtitle_text.stylize_before(border_style). stylize_before applies the combined panel+border style underneath the title's own spans, so the title inherits both the panel background and the border colour while its explicit style (e.g. red, magenta bold) still wins. Reasoning from the statement alone: 'title missing the panel background' plus 'reverts 7a38204' points at where the title gets its base style; `git show 7a38204` shows exactly the three lines to invert.
acceptable_alternatives: stylize_before(style) (panel style only, not the border colour) also passes both hidden tests, because the title's explicit colour overrides the border colour in the border-colour test. It differs from gold in that a title with no colour of its own would not pick up the border colour. Leaving the unused partial_border_style variable in place is harmless.
hidden_test_demands: tests/test_panel.py adds test_title_text_with_border_color (border_style='blue', title=Text('title', style='red'), subtitle=Text('subtitle', style='magenta bold'); expects title rendered '\x1b[31m title \x1b[0m' and subtitle '\x1b[1;35m subtitle \x1b[0m' between blue border segments) and test_title_text_with_panel_background (style='on blue'; expects '\x1b[31;44m title \x1b[0m' and '\x1b[1;35;44m subtitle \x1b[0m', i.e. the title keeps its colour AND gains bgcolor 44). Both compare exact ANSI strings at width=50, color_system='truecolor'. The existing test_render_panel, test_render_size and test_title_text must keep passing.
locating_signals: The title 'fix(panel)' and 'Panel title missing the panel background style' point to rich/panel.py, Panel.__rich_console__, at the title_text/subtitle_text stylize_before calls. 'reverts the change in 7a38204' names the exact commit to invert (git show 7a38204 works if history is present). The function is not named, but panel.py is small and 'title' plus 'style' greps land on the right lines immediately.
our_outcome_summary: v4, v6 and v8 passed; v7 failed. v6 and v8 match gold exactly (stylize_before(border_style) for title and subtitle) except that they leave the now-unused partial_border_style assignment. v4 used stylize_before(style) (panel style only), which passes both hidden tests but drops border-colour inheritance for uncoloured titles. v7 kept stylize_before(partial_border_style) and instead added a made-up `style=style` keyword to console.render(title_text, ...). Console.render() has no such parameter, so it raised TypeError: Console.render() got an unexpected keyword argument 'style', and 6 tests in tests/test_panel.py failed, including 3 existing ones (test_render_panel[panel5/panel6], test_render_size, test_title_text). Running the existing panel tests once would have caught this.
generalizable_lesson: When a PR-description statement says it 'reverts' or 'undoes' a named commit, run `git show <sha>` (or `git log -S` on the touched identifier) and invert that diff exactly rather than designing a new fix. Before adding a keyword argument to any existing function call, check that function's signature in the repo (grep 'def render(') because a guessed kwarg is a runtime TypeError. Always run the existing test file for the module you edited before you finish: a regression there means the patch is wrong, whatever the new behaviour looks like.
